# Problem

`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` derives the Conclusion verdict from the
**session's own** acceptance criteria only (`_derive_session_status()` at
`render_report.py:430-440`, called at `render_report.py:540`): all session ACs
`met` ⇒ `status = "completed"` ⇒ the Conclusion prints `✅ Ready to ship`
(`render_report.py:608-612`). The renderer already *knows* the audited work
item's verdict — `_audit_verdict()` (`render_report.py:344-371`) drives the
Meta-Data `Audit:` line and correctly reports `❌ failed` — but that knowledge
never reaches the Conclusion.

Result: an audit session whose work item's audit **failed** still ends with
`✅ Ready to ship` in the report, i.e. in the agent's final message to the
operator. Reported by the operator on 2026-11-16 after an audit run.

**Invariant to enforce: `✅ Ready to ship` may only be rendered when the audit
passed** (`auditResult.readyToClose == true`, equivalently the persisted
`Ready to close: Yes`).

# Live evidence (2026-11-16)

Audit session for `AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA` (Update Hangar War time budget: 5-15
minutes per hex, AI_Hell project). The persisted audit is `Ready to close: No`
(`auditResult.readyToClose: false`, auditedAt 2026-11-16T00:12:36Z). The
rendered report contained, in the same document:

```
## Meta-Data
...
- **Audit:** ❌ failed

## Conclusion

✅ Ready to ship
This completes the audit process for AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA (Update Hangar War time budget: 5-15 minutes per hex).
```

Reproduce with (from any checkout of this repo, project worklog auto-resolved):

```bash
python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA \
  --skill-name audit --headline "..." \
  --ac "Work item assessed against acceptance criteria|audit report|met" \
  --ac "Audit verdict determined and recorded|Ready to close line|met" \
  --ac "Ready-to-close line added|persisted audit report|met"
```

Operator impact: the last lines of a session — the part a producer actually
reads — can authorise shipping work whose audit failed. The Meta-Data line is
correct but sits far above the verdict and is easy to miss.

# Desired behaviour

1. When the report is rendered by the **audit** skill (`--skill-name audit`,
   case-insensitive), the Conclusion verdict is gated on the resolved audit
   verdict (`_audit_verdict(work_item, audit_result)`), in addition to the
   session ACs:
   - audit `yes` + every session AC `met` ⇒ `✅ Ready to ship` (today's text);
   - audit `no` ⇒ `🚫 Not ready to ship`, plus one reason line naming the
     verdict and the exact command to read the persisted report, e.g.
     `Audit verdict: Ready to close: No — see \`wl audit-show <id> --json\`.`;
   - audit `unknown` (no stored audit at all) ⇒ **not** ready (fail closed),
     reason line `Audit verdict: not run — no persisted audit for <id>.`
2. The header line (`# {status.title()} {skill_name}`) must agree with the
   Conclusion: no `# Completed audit` over a `🚫 Not ready to ship` verdict
   (it becomes `# Incomplete audit`, deriving from the gated status).
3. Both entry points apply the rule identically: the `wl`-backed path
   (`render_from_wl`, `render_report.py:688-730`, already forwards
   `audit_result=data.get("auditResult")`) and the `--json` stdin path
   (`render_report_from_workitem`).
4. **Non-audit skills are unchanged** — `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `test`,
   `refactor`, … byte-identical output to before this change (they have no
   audit verdict to consult and must not start failing closed).
5. No new `wl` calls: the verdict must come from data already fetched
   (`workItem.auditResult` / top-level `auditResult` / legacy `workItem.audit`).

# Key files

# Intake Brief: Do not require repeated producer reviews during release

## Problem statement

When a release re-audits work items (gate remediation, freshness re-runs), the
items are sometimes re-armed with `needsProducerReview`, so the producer is
asked to re-approve work the release itself has just touched. The desired rule
is simple: **require a producer review only when the audit failed for any
reason, or when code/content changed since the last review** — never because a
passing re-audit of unchanged work ran during a release.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — user story: "When I run a release I don't want the
  release's own re-audits to put passing, unchanged items back into my review
  queue; I only want to see genuine failures or actual changes."
- **Release engineer / automated release agent** — user story: "I want the
  producer-review flag to mean exactly 'the producer must look now', so the
  release gate neither blocks on already-reviewed unchanged work nor silently
  lets a failed item drop off the queue."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is
   set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or
   ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited
   content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of
   unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it.
2. **Failed ship-triggered re-audits still surface to the producer.** A
   ship-gate re-audit (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned `--ship-triggered` path)
   whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still sets `needsProducerReview` for
   the item to reach the producer queue; the ship-triggered carve-out
   suppresses only the passing/verification case. Where this diverges from
   SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ AC1 ('No' verdict leaves the flag untouched), the
   producer's stated rule in this item takes precedence and the divergence is
   reconciled (that item's Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer
   confirmation, which this item provides).
3. **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered
   suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a
   ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the
   last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit
   would.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code and lock: passing
   unchanged re-audit → no flag write; failed re-audit (independent and
   ship-triggered) → flag write; content change → flag write; marker absence
   → flag behaviour unchanged.
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document the
   only-when-failed-or-changed flag rule and the ship-triggered carve-out
   boundary (passing suppressed, failing/change still flagged).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers stop being asked to re-review work the release simply re-audited,
while genuine audit failures and real changes still land in their queue.

## Constraints

- **Independent audit behaviour unchanged.** Audits run outside release
  automation keep today's flag rules exactly (SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST,
  SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42, SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H preserve/required/untouched
  semantics); only ship-automated verification runs are touched.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour.** Suppression means "don't write the
  flag", never `--needs-producer-review no` retro-clearing; the ship close
  step's authorised override (SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q) is unchanged.
- **Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ before/while implementing.** That item
  is already planned (plan_complete); its 'No'-verdict suppression must be
  reconciled with AC2 of this item rather than silently shipping both.
- **Repository boundary.** Changes live in SorraAgents skills (audit, ship)
  and their docs; no herdr/ContextHub change required.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2745) resolves `preserved`/`required`/`untouched`;
  `_passing_audit_producer_decision()` (~line 2674) mirrors the passing
  verdict; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~line 17122) writes
  `--needs-producer-review yes` when `required`. Existing carve-outs: child
  items never flagged; cascade-demotion-suppressed 'No' untouched;
  tracked/accepted medium/low candidate-false-positive chores untouched.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`,
  `refresh-audits.js` — release-gate re-audit call sites that run
  `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict` (the SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ marker
  threading is planned but not yet implemented).
- Flag-rule precedents: SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST (preserve review across passing
  re-audits, flag independent failures), SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW (flag when
  automated audit says ready to close), SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H (top-level only).

## Desired change

- Confirm the producer-review flag rule as stated in AC1 and enforce it in the
  audit runner and the release flow: passing re-audits of unchanged items never
  set the flag; failing re-audits and content/code changes always do.
- Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ: its ship-triggered marker suppression
  covers the passing/verification case only; the failing-verdict case keeps
  flagging (or the divergence is explicitly recorded and producer-approved).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`

  the carve-out boundary.
- `skill/audit/tests/` (`test_audit_runner_producer_review.py`,
  `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`) — AC4 coverage.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ** — Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for
  producer review (open, plan_complete): the planned ship-triggered marker
  mechanism this item's rule constrains; reconciliation required (AC2).
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** — Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across
  passing re-audits; flag failing audits (completed): defines the
  preserved/required/untouched decision the release rule extends.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item as ready to close (completed): the foundational flag-on-yes rule.
- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (completed): child carve-out.
- **SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42** — audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every
  medium/low CFP chore (completed): CFP carve-out (same suppression spirit).
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — Ship skill: release-ready parent must override or
  absorb needsProducerReview on children (completed): close-step override kept
  out of scope here.
- **SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G** — Ship skill invalidates audits (open): adjacent
  freshness concern, distinct ACs.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
  (Producer-review flag lifecycle ~lines 444–542), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — contradictory ACs between items.** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned
  AC1 suppresses the flag for ship-triggered 'No' verdicts; AC2 of this item
  requires a failing ship-triggered re-audit to flag. Mitigation: this item
  records Blocked-by (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ) and the reconciliation is made
  explicit before either is implemented; if the producer prefers the
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ behaviour, AC2 is amended via that item's plan, not
  silently.
- **Risk — marker leakage** (from SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ): the ship-triggered
  marker must not be settable in an operator's shell. Mitigation: adopt the
  planned CLI-flag mechanism, never an env var.
- **Assumption — 'code was changed' = content-fingerprint change.** The only
  change signal the runner has today is the title/description content
  fingerprint; a repo/commits-change signal is out of scope (separate work
  item if desired).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Verdict semantics, close-step overrides, and the
  freshness/time-gate concerns of SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G are deliberately out of
  scope; they remain linked work items.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (failing ship-triggered re-audit):** Should a ship-gate
  re-audit whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still set
  `needsProducerReview`, or is demotion out of the release queue sufficient (as
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's plan assumes)? **Recommended (Map, intake): flag it /
  keep AC2 — this item's seed states the producer's rule that a producer review
  is required whenever the audit failed for any reason, and SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ
  Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer confirmation on exactly this point;
  this item is that confirmation.** Source: seed context of SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1
  ("We should only require a producer review if the audit failed for any
  reason, or if code was changed"), SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ Appendix Q2. Not
  independently re-confirmed (operator instructed no repeated producer reviews
  during this intake).
- **Assumption ("code was changed"):** "Code was changed" maps to the audit
  runner's existing content-fingerprint change signal (title/description
  content changed since the last review → fresh audit required), which is the
  only change signal the runner currently has; the item records the policy that
  this signal must keep arming the flag including for ship-triggered runs.
  A broader "repo/commits changed" signal would be a separate work item.
- **Assumption (relationship):** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ (already planned) is the
  implementation vehicle for the passing-verification suppression; this item
  carries the flag-rule policy and the failing/change boundary; the plan stage
  should reconcile the two (this item records Blocked-by SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ).

## Review log

- Completeness review: brief covers problem, users, ACs, constraints, existing
  state, desired change, key files, related work, appendix — no gaps found.
- Capture fidelity review: seed intent ('only require producer review when the
  audit failed for any reason, or if code was changed') preserved in AC1–AC3;
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ 'No'-verdict divergence recorded neutrally.
- Related-work & traceability review: all linked items verified against wl;
  typo SA-0MUJLWPB10038ZQ → SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q corrected.
- Risks & assumptions review: added Risks section (contradictory ACs, marker

- Polish & handoff review: wording tightened; commands are skill-standard.

  1. `SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5` — Test: audit_runner only-when-failed-or-changed producer review decision (leaf, no deps)

Log review shows repeated `cd` failures, reads against the main checkout while a

- AI agents: need a single command that prints the roots they must use, before any edit.

- `implement.py` commands resolve and validate the canonical worktree root before any git operation, through one helper used by every phase.

- Commands exit 2 with an actionable message naming the expected and resolved paths when the worktree is missing, is not a linked worktree, its `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` differs from the expected root, or the item prefix belongs to another project.

## Summary

shorthand, so agents stop re-parsing an undocumented payload and stop reaching for
full-suite runs during implementation.

Log review shows full runs that exceeded the per-command timeout, followed by broad
re-runs with longer timeouts, then repeated parsing of the JSON result to work out what
failed. `--scope changed`, `--group` and `--list-groups` already exist
(`SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51`), but the fast path is not the obvious default for iteration and
the JSON payload has no documented, versioned contract.

## Users

- AI agents iterating in implement sessions: need a fast command and a stable payload.
- The finish gate, audit cache and triage tools: need a contract that cannot drift.

- `run_tests.py` documents a stable JSON result schema and offers a fast scoped default: a `--fast` shorthand selects changed scope plus the unit profile, while explicit `--scope`/`--type` still win and the existing changed-scope fallback to full is preserved.

# Release gate treats a red build as non-fatal and never type-checks

## User story

As a producer, I want the dev→main release gate to refuse a tree that does not
build or type-check, so a broken release cannot be published.

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` verifies tests, but not types,
and does not treat a failed build as fatal. Two concrete defects:

1. **A red build is a warning, not a block.** The derived-version-file step runs
   the repo's build (`regenerate-version.js`) on the merged tree before tagging,
   but a failure only logs:
   `Warning: derived version file regeneration failed (continuing with release)`
   and the release proceeds (merge-dev-to-main.sh, "Regenerate derived version
   files" block). A tree whose build fails therefore still gets tagged, pushed
   and promoted.

2. **The full-suite gate does not type-check.** The only hard assertion is
   `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`. Every test runner in the
   framework (vitest, node --test, pytest) transpiles or interprets without
   type-checking, so a TypeScript type error yields a green suite. A repo that
   does not fail its build gate (defect 1) can ship code that does not compile.

Consequence (real incident, ContextHub v1.0.30): merge `485b764c7` resolved
conflicts by dropping code while leaving its consumers in place, producing 9
`TS2305`/`TS2724` errors in `packages/herdr`. The full suite was green, the
build step was non-fatal, and the broken tree was released to `main`.

The `implement.py finish` changed-scope gate has the same blind spot: it runs
tests, and tests do not typecheck.

## Desired change

- Make the release gate's build step **fatal**: a build failure on the merged
  tree blocks the release (exit non-zero before tagging), with an explicit
  documented bypass env var analogous to `SHIP_TEST_SKIP` for genuine
  emergencies.
- Add a build/type-check assertion to the release contract that is independent
  of the derived-version-file regeneration (they serve different purposes, and
  the regeneration step is legitimately non-fatal for *its own* purpose).
- Document the requirement so projects wire a `typecheck`/`build` script that
  covers their full source tree, including package subtrees (a root `tsc` with
  `include: ["src/**/*"]` does not cover `packages/*`).
- Consider surfacing the same check in the `implement.py finish` gate guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A release whose merged tree fails `npm run build` is blocked before tagging
  (verified with a throwaway failing-build commit on a scratch branch).
- The release remains able to complete when the build succeeds.
- Any bypass is explicit, documented and logged (mirroring `SHIP_TEST_SKIP`).
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` / `ship` skill docs describe the build gate and
  state that the full-suite gate does not substitute for type-checking.
- A project whose build does not cover package subtrees is called out in the
  docs as a project-side configuration error, not silently accepted.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing full-suite gate or its cache contract.
- The derived-version-file regeneration step keeps its own non-fatal semantics
  for *regeneration*; only a build *failure* becomes blocking.
- Existing projects without a `build` script must be unaffected.

**Key Files:**

- skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh
- skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js
- tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py
- skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs
- skill/ship/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/release-process.md
- docs/dev/release-tests.md
- docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md

## Implementation sketch (plan review)

Test-first, single vertical slice (no child items — effort Small / risk Low):

1. **Test first.** Add `tests/test_release_build_gate.py`, mirroring the
   established harness in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (throwaway
   repo with `main`/`dev` + bare `origin`, fake `gh`, isolated `HOME`):
   a failing-build fixture asserts a non-zero exit **before any tag exists**;
   a passing-build fixture asserts the release proceeds.
2. **Fatal build gate.** In `merge-dev-to-main.sh`, assert the repo's build
   (`package.json` `scripts.build`) on the merged tree as its own step —
   independent of derived-file regeneration, which keeps its non-fatal
   *regeneration* semantics. Runs after the tree-modifying steps and before
   the tag, alongside the full-suite gate. No `scripts.build` → no-op, so
   repos without a build are unaffected.
3. **Bypass.** Proposed `SHIP_BUILD_SKIP=1`, mirroring `SHIP_TEST_SKIP`:
   explicit, documented and logged when used.
4. **Docs.** `docs/dev/release-process.md` (the "Derived Version File
   Regeneration" section currently states a build failure never aborts the
   release — it must distinguish non-fatal *regeneration* from a blocking
   build *failure*), `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/release-tests.md`,
   `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`: describe the build gate, state that
   the full-suite gate does not substitute for type-checking, and call out a
   project build that misses package subtrees (e.g. a root `tsc` whose
   `include` omits `packages/*`) as a project-side configuration error.
5. **Optional, docs only.** One guidance line in
   `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` noting that the `finish`
   changed-scope gate runs tests, not type-checks (see OPEN QUESTION in the
   plan Appendix — non-blocking; no change to `implement.py` gate logic).

## Impact

A release can no longer publish a tree that fails to build, so a broken build
stops at the release gate instead of reaching users.

merge `485b764c7`, which shipped in v1.0.30.

Refactor-filed work items carry machine-readable identity markers (`Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:`, `Refactor-Affected-Lines:`) injected at the top of their description.
